homepage_url_justification: Project homepage is the GitLab repository https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder (also linked from DESCRIPTION URL, alongside the CRAN page https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=punycoder). The pkgdown documentation site is being republished on GitLab Pages and will be named here once it is live.
sites_https_justification: All project sites are served over HTTPS: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder and https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=punycoder .
description_good_justification: DESCRIPTION and README provide a clear, succinct description of what punycoder does: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/README.md
interact_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains how to interact with and contribute to the project: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the requirements for acceptable contributions (tests, passing lint via the .lintr style config, and the GitLab CI merge gate -- the lint, readme, news-version, check and coverage jobs): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
license_location_justification: LICENSE is at the repository top level: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/LICENSE
floss_license_osi_justification: MIT is an OSI-approved open source license: https://opensource.org/license/mit
documentation_basics_justification: Basic documentation in the README (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/README.md) plus package vignettes (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/tree/main/vignettes) and the architecture and decision notes (ARCHITECTURE.md, DECISIONS.md) at the repository root.
documentation_interface_justification: Every exported function is documented with roxygen2; the generated Rd pages are in the repository (https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/tree/main/man) and are rendered by CRAN at https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=punycoder .
repo_track_justification: All changes are tracked in git: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/commits/main
repo_interim_justification: Interim development commits are publicly available on GitLab between releases: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/commits/main
repo_distributed_justification: Uses git, a distributed version control system: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder
version_unique_justification: Each release carries a unique version (DESCRIPTION Version; CRAN enforces uniqueness): https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=punycoder
version_semver_justification: Uses semantic-style x.y.z versioning; release tags visible at https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/tags
version_tags_justification: Releases are tagged in git (vX.Y.Z) and distributed through CRAN: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/tags
release_notes_justification: NEWS.md documents user-facing changes for each release: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/NEWS.md
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerabilities have been fixed to date; NEWS.md records all changes: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/NEWS.md
report_tracker_justification: GitLab Issues serve as the bug tracker: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/issues
report_process_justification: Users submit bug reports through the GitLab issue tracker, which offers a Bug issue template (.gitlab/issue_templates/Bug.md): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/issues
report_responses_justification: Maintainer responds to issue reports on the tracker: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/issues
enhancement_responses_justification: Maintainer responds to enhancement requests on the tracker, which offers a Feature issue template (.gitlab/issue_templates/Feature.md): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/issues
report_archive_justification: GitLab Issues provide a publicly available, searchable archive of reports and responses: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/issues/?state=all
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: The vulnerability-reporting process is published in the security policy: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/SECURITY.md . Reports go to the maintainer by email, with a confidential GitLab issue as a documented alternative.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Two confidential channels are documented in SECURITY.md: email to the maintainer, and a GitLab confidential issue (tick 'This issue is confidential' at https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/issues/new ), which is visible only to project maintainers. GitHub private vulnerability reporting no longer applies -- the project is not hosted on GitHub.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: SECURITY.md commits to acknowledging reports within 7 days and coordinating a fix and disclosure: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/SECURITY.md
build_justification: Builds with the standard R toolchain (R CMD build / INSTALL, devtools) plus the configure script that detects libidn2: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/configure
build_common_tools_justification: Uses the standard, widely available R build tooling plus a POSIX configure script.
build_floss_tools_justification: R, GCC/Clang, and the entire build toolchain are free/open source software: https://www.r-project.org/
test_invocation_justification: Tests run via devtools::test() and as part of R CMD check.
test_most_justification: Coverage is measured with covr in the `coverage` CI job and published through GitLab's native coverage reporting (pipeline coverage badge, merge-request coverage diff, and per-file annotations from the Cobertura report): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/pipelines
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires tests for new features and bug fixes: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
tests_are_added_justification: New functionality ships with tests, enforced in review.
tests_documented_added_justification: The test-addition policy is documented in CONTRIBUTING.md: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
warnings_justification: Warnings are surfaced via R CMD check and lintr in CI (the `lint` and `check` jobs): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
warnings_fixed_justification: Warnings are treated as errors and fixed; R CMD check is kept clean.
warnings_strict_justification: The `lint` CI job sets LINTR_ERROR_ON_LINT=true so any lint fails the build, and `check` runs rcmdcheck with error_on = "warning": https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer applies secure design principles; punycoder defensively handles untrusted Punycode/IDNA input through its C/C++ codec core, enforcing length limits, valid UTF-8, and label-structure rules.
know_common_errors_justification: The maintainer is aware of common C/C++ memory-safety and IDNA parsing pitfalls (buffer overflows, integer overflows, homograph attacks). The C++ codec core is covered by clang-ASAN/UBSAN and valgrind in dynamic analysis.
crypto_password_storage_justification: punycoder stores no passwords or credentials.
crypto_random_justification: punycoder does not generate security-sensitive random values.
crypto_used_network_justification: punycoder is a string/IDNA library and does not itself make network connections.
crypto_tls12_justification: punycoder does not establish network connections.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: punycoder does not establish network connections.
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: punycoder does not establish network connections.
delivery_mitm_justification: Distributed via CRAN and GitLab over HTTPS; CRAN publishes per-package checksums: https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=punycoder
delivery_unsigned_justification: All distribution downloads are served over HTTPS (CRAN and GitLab): https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=punycoder
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No outstanding known vulnerabilities; tracker at https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/issues
static_analysis_justification: lintr (full-package lint), R CMD check, and goodpractice are run; FOSSA and Socket scan dependencies: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: R CMD check plus lintr cover common defect classes; FOSSA/Socket cover dependency vulnerabilities; R CMD check --as-cran (the `full-check` job) flags C/C++ compiler warnings: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
static_analysis_fixed_justification: Static-analysis findings are addressed before merge.
static_analysis_often_justification: lintr runs on every CI build (each push to main and each merge request): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
dynamic_analysis_justification: Before releases the `sanitizers` CI job runs R CMD check — including the testthat suite — inside R-hub's clang-ASAN/UBSAN and valgrind container images (ghcr.io/r-hub/containers/clang-asan and .../valgrind), exercising the C/C++ Punycode/IDNA codec core: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: punycoder ships C/C++ code in src/ (the RFC 3492 Punycode encoder/decoder and UTS #46 normalizer). The `sanitizers` CI job runs the package under clang-ASAN/UBSAN (memory errors and undefined behaviour) and valgrind (memory leaks and illegal memory access) before releases, using R-hub's published container images: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: punycoder's automated test suite uses testthat, whose expectations (expect_*) are assertions checked at runtime during dynamic analysis on every CI run: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/tree/main/tests/testthat . The `sanitizers` CI job additionally runs the package under the clang-ASAN/UBSAN and valgrind configurations, enabling runtime memory and undefined-behaviour assertions over the C/C++ codec core: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: Any issues surfaced by the sanitizer or valgrind runs are fixed before release.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitLab CI/CD runs lint + README-sync + NEWS/version + R CMD check + coverage on every push to main and every merge request: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/pipelines (configuration: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/.gitlab-ci.yml )
discussion_justification: GitLab Issues provide a public forum for project discussion: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/issues
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credentials are committed to the repository; Socket and FOSSA scan the repo: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder
english_justification: Documentation and issue-tracker interaction are conducted in English (Language: en-US): https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/blob/main/README.md
hardening_justification: Hardening mechanisms (e.g. HTTP security headers) apply to web applications; punycoder is an R library.
sites_password_security_justification: Project sites (GitLab, CRAN) manage their own authentication; punycoder operates no site with user passwords.
maintained_justification: Actively maintained: recent CRAN releases, frequent commits, and responsive issue handling: https://gitlab.com/bart-turczynski/punycoder/-/commits/main
